prices.title: Load SMARD auction prices
prices.input: Weekly quarter-hour JSON series from Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de, for the Germany–Luxembourg bidding zone. Values are in €/MWh.
prices.operation: Parse delivery timestamps into UTC, check duplicates and retain negative prices. A price below zero is a market outcome, not a missing value.
prices.output: Earlier eligible prices supply lag features and training labels. Delivery-day outcomes are joined separately for evaluation.

snapshot.title: Check and save auction prices
snapshot.input: SMARD auction prices and the timing evidence that came with them.
snapshot.operation: Validate units, quarter-hour timestamps and coverage. Save a fixed copy so later runs use exactly the same prices.
snapshot.output: A frozen price snapshot and its recorded timing evidence.
snapshot.technical: The price snapshot uses a typed Parquet table. A manifest identifies the source and records the file checksum so the saved inputs can be verified.

select.title: Select inputs available by 11:00 Berlin
select.input: Auction prices with delivery, publication and retrieval times kept distinct.
select.operation: For each delivery date, apply the preceding day’s 11:00 Berlin cutoff to the recorded price versions under the declared timing assumptions. Stop on unexpected gaps in the required price history.
select.output: The earlier prices eligible for that day’s forecast, with the price timing assumptions recorded.

features.title: Prepare one set of model inputs per quarter-hour
features.input: Eligible auction price history and the German local calendar.
features.operation: Use prices from the same local quarter-hour 1, 2, 7 and 14 days earlier, plus daily price summaries. Add the quarter of day, weekday, month and holidays. Average duplicate lag quarters on the autumn clock-change day and flag lags that did not exist in spring.
features.output: One row of price and calendar inputs per physical delivery quarter.

labels.title: Choose past prices to learn from
labels.input: Realised prices for delivery dates before the monthly fit.
labels.operation: Use only price versions known by 11:00 Berlin on the day before the first delivery day being evaluated that month. Each past day’s model inputs still use that day’s original information deadline; later revisions cannot replace them.
labels.output: Past inputs paired with prices the model can learn from. Prices for the month being evaluated are reserved for scoring predictions afterwards.

fit.title: Train the prices/calendar model once a month
fit.input: Eligible past examples with price and calendar inputs and realised auction prices.
fit.operation: Fit the same model settings each month, expanding training with the newly eligible history. Each past day’s inputs keep its original information deadline.
fit.output: One fitted CatBoost model reused for every forecast day in the month.
fit.technical: CatBoost combines decision trees and learns five percentiles by penalising over- and under-prediction differently for each percentile. Local Metaflow execution preserves the archived code, locked runtime and exact input snapshot.

predict.title: Estimate prices and uncertainty for each quarter-hour
predict.input: The delivery day’s prepared inputs, the fitted model and the calibrated reference.
predict.operation: Predict five price percentiles with CatBoost and sort them if they cross. Calculate the reference from earlier same-clock auction prices and its training-only error adjustments. Stop if a required input or prediction is missing.
predict.output: Five percentiles: 2.5%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 97.5%. The middle estimate is the median; the outer pairs form the 50% and 95% uncertainty bands. These describe each quarter-hour separately, not how prices move together across the day.

truth.title: Join realised prices after prediction
truth.input: Realised SMARD auction prices for evaluated delivery quarters.
truth.operation: Match both forecasts to the actual price for the same delivery time, using UTC to distinguish repeated clock times in autumn. Scoring requires an actual price for every registered delivery quarter.
truth.output: Matched forecast/outcome rows for evaluation, without feeding outcomes back into historical prediction.

score.title: Score every method on matching outcomes
score.input: The prices/calendar model and the reference, paired with the same complete realised price grid.
score.operation: Measure errors in the middle price estimate, band width, and how often actual prices fall inside the bands. Weighted interval score balances narrow bands against penalties for missed prices. Summarise by day, month and full period. Use the recorded block length in days to estimate uncertainty in the full-period score difference.
score.output: Comparable results with sample counts and limitations. A lower score does not by itself establish reliable bands, live readiness or trading value.

reference.title: Set up the simple comparison forecast
reference.input: Earlier same-clock prices and training-period forecast errors, available before the monthly fit cutoff.
reference.operation: Average yesterday’s and last week’s price for the same local quarter-hour. Use one if the other is absent; if both are missing, use the middle value from earlier prices at that time of day. Set the uncertainty bands using only errors from the training period. Keep those band adjustments fixed during the month.
reference.output: A separate reference forecast with five quantiles per quarter. It provides a comparison for the fitted baseline.

models.title: Reuse the model and reference calibration throughout the month
models.input: The fitted CatBoost model and the reference error adjustments.
models.operation: Update the daily inputs and apply the same monthly model and reference adjustments. The evaluated month’s outcomes enter scoring after prediction.
models.output: Methods ready to forecast each day from the information available by its deadline.

output.title: Five price estimates for every quarter-hour tomorrow
output.operation: Retain the 2.5th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 97.5th percentiles in €/MWh. The 50th is the median estimate; the 25th–75th form the central 50% band and the 2.5th–97.5th form the central 95% band. These nominal bands need measured coverage.
output.output: A next-day price curve and uncertainty bands: normally 96 quarters, or 92/100 on clock-change days. This viewer shows saved historical forecasts, not a live service. Each quarter’s uncertainty is separate; the bands are not joint daily scenarios.
